newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 19.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- CITY WATCHDOG URGES WIDE REFORM

Sir Andrew Large, London's chief regulator is proposing a reform of the city's financial regulation as a means of heightening efficiency and ensuring directors are held responsible for their own losses. Lane sees the current system to be lacking "efficiency and credibility" and defined by "inconsistency, operational expense, and duplication and delays". The regulator intends to ensure that investors responsible for mis-selling personal pensions in the 1980's and 1990's to thousands of investors are held accountable.
-- BOEING LINK-UP COULD BE RULED 'ILLEGAL' BY EU

The European Union has warned privately that the proposed merger of Boeing and McDonnell Douglas could be declared "illegal", or the new group could face a fine of around five billion dollars if the two U.S. firms ignore the EU's concerns about the impact on competition. The EU has formulated a list of objections to the deal which it will send out this week, leading to talk that it will add to existing transatlantic tensions about the proposed merger.
-- LONRHO AND JCI IN MERGER TALKS

South African mining house JCI has entered "exploratory" merger talks with London-listed conglomerate Lonrho in the hope of creating a two billion sterling mining group. If the merger takes place, it would allow Anglo American, the largest Lonrho shareholder, to acquire Lonrho's 33 per cent stake in Ashanti Goldfields. The merger could also double JCI's coal mining interests, adding platinum to its business.
-- EASYJET'S OWNER WANTS TO BUY LUTON AIRPORT

Stelios Haji-Ioannou, owner of budget airline Easyjet, is in talks with the Luton Borough Council over plans to purchase Luton airport, which is valued at between 50 and 100 million sterling. The Luton council, however, had planned to invest its own money, as the airport is in need of extra funding for expansion, and will allow it to become a commercial entity only if it remains wholly owned by the council. Analysts believe that anything is possible under Labour and have not ruled out the sale.
-- TASKFORCE DOES BATTLE TO KEEP THE LINES OPEN

After 18 months of work, Mercury engineers have equipped a mobile task force to provide and maintain telecommunications for relief workers in disaster areas. A similar 1.2 million sterling project by Cable & Wireless Emergency Response Unit, named Land Rovers, is currently being used in areas such as Bosnia and Rwanda on a non-profit basis. C&W's ERU is an easy-to-use device which can be assembled and maintained even by those untrained in the telecoms sector.
-- UTILITIES CLAIM FAIR SHARE OF WINDFALL TAX

Figures distributed by PowerGen to The Treasury indicate that British Telecommunications and the electricity generators should pay less windfall tax than other utilities, as the groups were sold off in tranches, with returns distributed evenly between the companies and shareholders. PowerGen does not dispute that the government can levy a windfall tax, but believe any calculation for the tax should take all "exceptional circumstances" into consideration.
-- BIOTECH FUNDS LAUNCHED

Specialist investment trusts are planning to raise over 60 million sterling on London's Stock Exchange to invest in Europe's increasingly popular biotechnology sector. Through the trusts, companies will be able to invest in state-of-the-art technology and struggling companies will be provided insurance against risks. The U.S. is currently home to most of the world's biotechnology sectors, but growth has recently been stronger in Europe.
-- GALEN SEEKS 20 MILLION STERLING TO FUND DRUGS EXPANSION

Northern Ireland pharmaceuticals company Galen has announced plans to float on the stock market and to expand its Clinical Trials Supplies subsidiary which organises packaging and distribution of new drugs to be used in patient trials. The CTS business accounts for 30 per cent of Galen's turnover and is the supplier to most of the major pharmaceuticals companies. The listing of Galen is hoped to raise about 20 million sterling which will be used to fund most of the expansion.
-- ORACLE HOTS UP INTERNET RIVALRY

Oracle, the second largest software company in the world, is expected to announce that it will soon acquire a controlling interest in software developer Navio Communications. It is believed that Oracle will use Navio, a developer of software which enables TV and video game players to access the Internet, to create its new line of Internet "network computer" terminals, which are less expensive than normal personal computers.
-- QUEUE FOR CHINESE CAR SALE

Jacques Calvet, chairman of Peugeot-Citroen has said he expects to announce the successful bidder for the company's divested 22 per cent in Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile "very shortly". The bid for the stake in one of China's first carmaking joint ventures has received a tremendous amount of interest, with leading contenders being BMW, Hyundai, Honda and General Motors' Opel subsidiary. Some see the amount of interest as surprising due to a recent depression in the Chinese car market and the past troubles at the joint venture.
